title: What the Site's Cafe Counter Adds to the Pot
content:
The counter run under the Workplace Cafe Management Program contract at an Employee Meal Account's site may itself put something into the pot a ticket draws on, and what it puts in follows the funding model that contract's service model publishes.

**Clause.** Where the employer's cafe programme at the account's site stands active and funds meals at a fixed amount for each meal, the employer's counter adds the per employee daily subsidy that programme publishes. Where the employer's cafe programme at the account's site stands active and funds meals at a percentage of the menu price, the employer's counter adds that published percentage of the ticket, rounded to two decimal places at that step. Where neither holds, the employer's counter adds nothing.

## The bands

| The cafe contract at the account's site | How its service model funds meals | Added to the pot |
|---|---|---|
| Active | A fixed amount for each meal | The per employee daily subsidy that programme publishes |
| Active | A percentage of the menu price | That published percentage of the ticket |
| Active | On any other basis | Nothing |
| In any other state, or none held at the site | Any | Nothing |

The ticket the percentage is taken of is the largest meal rung against payroll on the account.

*Hypothetical illustration.* An active cafe contract funding meals at a fixed amount for each meal and publishing $9.00 a day for one employee adds $9.00 to the pot. An active contract funding at 35 percent of the menu price, against a ticket of $16.00, adds $5.60. A contract at the site standing suspended adds nothing on either model.
